patch.value: Reference extension claimed to be fully typed but used any, hiding three wrong SDK contracts

value.author: claude
value.text: This package is the reference extension for all 9 SDK capabilities and its manifest description ends "all fully typed", but every register* helper took api: any and every handler took ctx: any. Typing them against the real SDK types immediately surfaced three contract violations that the any had been absorbing.

value.author: claude
value.text: DEFECT 1 - search provider returned { results: items }. The contract is SearchProviderHit[] | { hits }, where a hit is { id, score }, not a raw item. Every caller of this demo provider got zero hits. DEFECT 2 - vector store query returned { results: [...] } where the contract is a bare VectorStoreQueryHit[]. DEFECT 3 - the onIndex hook logged ctx.count and ctx.path; OnIndexHookContext has neither (it has mode and total_items), so the demo logged undefined.

value.author: claude
value.text: DEFECT 4 (found while removing the now-orphaned buffer helpers): runPm - the single shell-out every demo command uses - passed no maxBuffer, so it inherited Nodes 1 MiB default. An overrun kills the child with status null and EMPTY stderr, so the failure was invisible. The pmJsonMaxBuffer/describePmReadFailure helpers already existed but were wired only into the search provider; they are now in runPm where the shell-outs actually are.

value.author: claude
value.text: The search provider no longer shells out at all: SearchProviderQueryContext already carries ctx.documents, so the old implementation spawned a pm subprocess per query for data the host had already supplied. Tests now activate through the SDK host harness (createExtensionTestHarness) instead of a hand-written api double, which enforces manifest capability governance a stub cannot.

patch.value: Typed against real SDK contracts; four defects fixed and covered by tests
